nodes.name: Graded space / algebra / module
nodes.statement: A vector $k$-space, $k$-algebra, or $k$-algebra module is called graded if it is $\mathbb{Z}_+$-graded and finite-dimensional in every component. The Hilbert series is $V(x) = \sum_{i \geq 0} \dim V_i \, x^i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Graded means non-negatively graded with finite-dimensional components; Hilbert series is the generating function of component dimensions.

nodes.name: Connected and standard graded algebra
nodes.statement: A graded algebra $A = A_0 \oplus A_1 \oplus \dots$ is called connected if $A_0 = k$; a connected algebra is called standard if it is generated by $A_1$ and a unit.

nodes.name: Strongly free (inert) set
nodes.statement: A set $\alpha \subset A$ of homogeneous elements is called strongly free (or inert) if equality holds in the Golod-Shafarevich-type Hilbert series inequality $(B \ast k\langle\alpha\rangle)(t) \geq A(t)$, where $B = A/\mathrm{id}(\alpha)$. For $A$ free, this is equivalent to $\mathrm{gl.dim}\, A/\mathrm{id}(\alpha) \leq 2$.

nodes.name: Exponent of growth $p(A)$
nodes.statement: For a graded algebra $A$ with $a_i = \dim A_i$, define $p(A) = \inf\{q > 0 \mid \exists c > 0 \; \forall n \geq 0,\; a_n \leq c q^n\}$. Equivalently, $p(A) = \lim \sqrt[n]{a_n} = r(A)^{-1}$.
nodes.notes: Analogue of Gelfand-Kirillov dimension; depends on the chosen grading.

nodes.name: Radius of convergence $r(A)$
nodes.statement: For a graded algebra $A$, $r(A)$ denotes the radius of convergence of the Hilbert series $A(t)$.

nodes.name: Extremal algebra
nodes.statement: A graded algebra $A$ is said to be extremal if for every nonzero homogeneous ideal $I \triangleleft A$ we have $r(A/I) > r(A)$ (equivalently, $p(A/I) < p(A)$ for every proper quotient).

nodes.name: Undecidable pair $(s,t)$
nodes.statement: A pair of integers $(s,t)$ is called undecidable if there is no algorithm that, given a set $\alpha \subset F_s$ of $t$ homogeneous quadratic elements, decides in finitely many steps whether $\alpha$ is strongly free.
nodes.notes: Existence of undecidable pairs is established in Anick [A2].

nodes.name: Overlap of monomials
nodes.statement: A non-empty monomial $a$ is an overlap of two monomials $b, c$ if there exist non-empty monomials $f, g$ such that $b = f a$ and $c = a g$.

nodes.name: Chain of rank $n$ and its tail
nodes.statement: For a free algebra $F = k\langle X\rangle$ with monomial ideal $I$ generated by $U$, define chains by induction: every $x \in X$ is a chain of rank 0 (its own tail). For $n > 0$, $f = g t$ is a chain of rank $n$ with tail $t$ if (i) $g$ is a chain of rank $n-1$, (ii) for the tail $r$ of $g$, $rt = vu$ with $u \in U$, and (iii) excluding $u$ as the end, no subword of $rt$ lies in $U$.

nodes.name: Hilbert series identity from minimal resolution
nodes.statement: There is an equality of formal power series $R(x)\bigl(1 - sx + u(x) - H_3(x) + \dots + (-1)^i H_i(x)\bigr) = 1 + (-1)^i \Omega_i(x)$. In particular, $R(x)(1 - H_0(x) + \dots - H_{2i-1}(x)) \geq 1$ and $R(x)(1 - H_0(x) + \dots + H_{2i}(x)) \leq 1$, with equality iff $\mathrm{gl.dim}\, R \leq 2i-1$ (resp. $\leq 2i$).
assumptions: $R$ is a standard graded associative algebra $F/I$
$\Omega_i = \mathrm{Coker}\, d_{i-1}$ from a minimal free $R$-resolution of $k$

nodes.name: Golod-Shafarevich theorem
nodes.statement: There is an inequality $R(x)(1 - sx + u(x)) \geq 1$. Equality holds iff $\mathrm{gl.dim}\, R \leq 2$ (equivalently, $\alpha$ is strongly free / inert).
assumptions: $R = F/I$ where $F = k\langle x_1,\dots,x_s\rangle$ is free
nodes.notes: Inequality due to Golod-Shafarevich [GSh]; equality condition due to Anick [A1].

nodes.name: Identification of $\Omega_3$ with a Tor module
nodes.statement: Let $L = F\alpha$ be the left ideal of $F$ generated by $\alpha$. There is an isomorphism of left $R$-modules $\Omega_3 \cong \mathrm{Tor}^F_1(R, P/L)$.

nodes.name: Strongly free criterion via Tor
nodes.statement: The non-empty set $\alpha$ is strongly free iff $\mathrm{Tor}^F_1(R, P/L) = 0$.

nodes.name: Section 2 results extend to connected algebras
nodes.statement: All results of Section 2 hold for an arbitrary connected algebra $R$; one only replaces the term $sx$ with the generating function $\sum_{i \geq 1} t^{\deg x_i}$ in the algebra's generators.

nodes.name: Govorov's inequalities for the number of relations
nodes.section: 3 Estimates for the number of relations
nodes.statement: If $I$ is minimally generated by $t > 0$ elements of degree $l$, then $R(x)$ converges at $x = s^{-1}$, and (3) $t \geq s^l / R(s^{-1})$, (4) $t \geq (s a_{n-1} - a_n)/a_{n-l}$ for all admissible $n$. Equality holds in (4) for all $n$ iff $\mathrm{Tor}^F_1(R, P/L) = 0$.

nodes.name: Govorov bound (3)
nodes.section: 3 Estimates for the number of relations
nodes.statement: $t \geq \dfrac{s^l}{R(s^{-1})}$.

nodes.name: Govorov bound (4)
nodes.section: 3 Estimates for the number of relations
nodes.statement: $t \geq \dfrac{s a_{n-1} - a_n}{a_{n-l}}$ for all admissible $n$.

nodes.name: Coincidence of equality cases (Theorem 6)
nodes.section: 3 Estimates for the number of relations
nodes.statement: The following are equivalent: (i) $\alpha$ is strongly free; (ii) equality holds in Govorov's inequality (3); (iii) equality holds in Govorov's inequality (4) for all admissible $n$.
assumptions: Setup of Section 3: $\alpha$ minimal homogeneous of common degree $l$ in free $F$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6
nodes.section: 3 Estimates for the number of relations
nodes.statement: Combine Corollary 4 with Theorem 5 for (i) $\Leftrightarrow$ (iii); for (i) $\Leftrightarrow$ (ii), substitute $x = s^{-1}$ in the Golod-Shafarevich inequality with $u(x) = t x^l$.

nodes.name: Implications via Cor. 4 and Govorov
nodes.statement: (i) $\Leftrightarrow$ (iii) follows immediately from Corollary 4 (strong freeness $\iff$ $\mathrm{Tor}^F_1(R, P/L) = 0$) and Theorem 5 (equality in (4) $\iff$ same Tor vanishes).

nodes.name: Substitute $x = s^{-1}$ in Golod-Shafarevich
nodes.statement: With $u(x) = t x^l$, the inequality (2) at $x = s^{-1}$ becomes $R(s^{-1}) t s^{-l} \geq 1$, equivalent to (3); equality in (2) gives equality in (3).

nodes.name: Strict converse
nodes.statement: If $\alpha$ is not strongly free then $R(x)(1 - sx + t x^l) \geq 1 + a x^n$ with $a > 0$; substituting $x = s^{-1}$ gives $R(s^{-1}) t s^{-l} \geq 1 + a s^{-n} > 1$, hence $t > s^l/R(s^{-1})$.

nodes.name: Properties of radii of convergence
nodes.statement: (i) $r(A) = \infty$ iff $A$ is finite-dimensional. (ii) If $A$ is finitely generated then $r(A) > 0$. (iii) $r(A) = 1$ iff $A$ is infinite-dimensional with sub-exponential growth. (iv) If $B$ is a sub- or quotient algebra of $A$ then $r(B) \geq r(A)$. (v) If $r(A) > 0$ then $\lim_{t \to r(A)} A(t) = \infty$; for $A$ connected, $f(t) = A(t)^{-1}$ is continuous on $[0, r(A)]$ with $f(0) = 1$, $f(r(A)) = 0$.

nodes.name: Undecidability lifts to larger rank
nodes.statement: Let $l$ be a positive integer and $(s,t)$ an undecidable pair. Then $(s+l, t)$ is undecidable.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8
nodes.statement: Let $G = F \ast k\langle x_{s+1},\dots,x_{s+l}\rangle$. Then $\alpha \subset F$ is strongly free in $F$ iff it is strongly free in $G$, so undecidability transfers.

nodes.name: Quadratic strongly free counts double
nodes.statement: Let $s$ be even. If the pair $(s,t)$ is undecidable, then so is $(2s, s^2/4)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9
nodes.statement: By [A4], a quadratic strongly free set in $F$ of $q$ elements exists iff $4q \leq s^2$, so $t \leq s^2/4$. Choose a quadratic strongly free $\beta$ in $k\langle x_{s+1},\dots,x_{2s}\rangle$ with $s^2/4 - t$ elements; then $\alpha \cup \beta$ is strongly free in $F \ast G$ iff $\alpha$ is strongly free in $F$.

nodes.name: $(4d, d^2)$ undecidable for large $d$
nodes.statement: For large enough integer $d$, the pair $(4d, d^2)$ is undecidable.

nodes.name: Undecidability of Hilbert-series equalities
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{char}\, k = 0$ and $F_s$ free of rank $s$. (i) For undecidable $(s,t)$, no algorithm decides whether $R(s^{-1}) = s^2/t$ when $\alpha \subset F_s$ is a set of $t$ quadratic elements and $R = F_s/\mathrm{id}(\alpha)$. (ii) For some integers $s, t, q$, no algorithm decides whether $r(R) = q^{-1}$ when $\gamma \subset F_s$ is given; for large $d$ one may take $s = 64d$, $t = 241 d^2$, $q = 60 d$.
assumptions: $F_s$ free associative of rank $s$ with standard grading
conclusions: Undecidability of $r(R) = q^{-1}$ for explicit $s, t, q$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 11
nodes.statement: Part (i) follows from Theorem 6 and Corollary 10. For (ii), construct $C = A \ast B$ from a free $A = k\{1, y_1,\dots,y_{4d}\}$ with $y_i y_j = 0$ and $B = F_{60d}/\mathrm{id}(\alpha)$, then compute $C^{-1}(x)$ and use Proposition 7(v).

nodes.name: Reduce (i) to Theorem 6 and Corollary 10
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 6 (equality in Govorov $\Leftrightarrow$ strongly free) together with Corollary 10 (undecidability of $(4d, d^2)$ scaled to quadratic case).

nodes.name: Construct $C = A \ast B$ for part (ii)
nodes.statement: Choose $d$ with $(60d, 152 d^2)$ undecidable; let $\alpha$ have $152 d^2$ quadratic elements in $F_{60d}$, $B = F_{60d}/\mathrm{id}(\alpha)$, $A = k\langle y_1,\dots,y_{4d}\mid y_i y_j = 0\rangle$, then $C \cong A \ast B$ has $s = 64d$ generators and $t = (4d)^2 + 152 d^2 = 241 d^2$ quadratic relations.

nodes.name: Contradiction when $\alpha$ is not strongly free
nodes.statement: If $\alpha$ is not strongly free, Theorem 6 gives $B^{-1}((60d)^{-1}) < 1/16$, hence $C^{-1}((60d)^{-1}) < 0$, contradicting Proposition 7(v); thus $r(C) \neq (60d)^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Extremal implies finite positive radius
nodes.statement: If $A$ is an extremal algebra, then $0 < r(A) < \infty$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 12
nodes.statement: Suppose $r(A) = 0$. Pick a nonzero homogeneous $a \in A$ of degree $d$, set $I = (a)$, $B = A/I$, $F = k\langle c \mid \deg c = d\rangle$. Then $(B \ast F)(t) \geq A(t)$ forces $r(B \ast F) = 0$. But $(B \ast F)(t)^{-1} = b(t)^{-1} - dt$ is analytic near zero with value 1, giving $r(B \ast F) > 0$, contradiction.

nodes.name: Extremal algebras are prime
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be an extremal algebra. Then $A$ is prime.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 13
nodes.statement: Reduce to: for nonzero homogeneous ideals $I, J$ with $J = (a)$ principal of degree $h$, if $IJ = 0$ then writing $A = I \oplus V$ gives $J(t) \leq t^h + 2 t^h V(t) + t^h V(t)^2$, hence $A(t) \leq C(t) + t^h (B(t)+1)^2$, yielding $r(A) \geq \min\{r(B), r(C)\}$ contradicting extremality.

nodes.name: Refined identity in proof of Theorem 13
nodes.statement: For any homogeneous ideals $I, J$ of a graded algebra $A$, if $IJ = 0$ then $r(A) = \min\{r(A/I), r(A/J)\}$.

nodes.name: Filtered algebras with extremal $\mathrm{gr}\, A$ are prime
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be a (non-graded) locally finite filtered algebra such that the associated graded $\mathrm{gr}\, A$ is extremal. Then $A$ is prime.

nodes.name: Free product of connected algebras is extremal
nodes.statement: Let $A, B$ be non-trivial connected algebras with $r(A) > 0$ and $r(B) > 0$. Then $A \ast B$ is extremal.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 15
nodes.statement: Set $C = A \ast B$; $C(t)^{-1} = A(t)^{-1} + B(t)^{-1} - 1$ is analytic near 0, so $r(C) > 0$. Reduce to monomial case via Grobner bases. For a nonzero monomial principal ideal $S$, use Lemma 16 to find $p$, build the chain decomposition of $D = C/P$, compute $D(t)^{-1} = C(t)^{-1} - C'(-1, t)$, and show $D(r(C))^{-1} > 0$, hence $r(D) > r(C)$.

nodes.name: Positivity of $r(C)$ via free-product formula
nodes.statement: Since $C(t)^{-1} = A(t)^{-1} + B(t)^{-1} - 1$ is analytic and equals 1 at 0, $r(C) > 0$ and $r(C) < \min\{r(A), r(B)\}$.

nodes.name: Reduce to monomial algebras via Grobner bases
nodes.statement: Standard Grobner-basis argument: pass to associated monomial algebras $\bar A, \bar B$; for any homogeneous ideal $I \triangleleft C$ there exists $J \triangleleft \bar C$ with $r(C/I) \geq r(\bar C/J)$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 16 to choose monomial $p$
nodes.statement: Use Lemma 16 to obtain a monomial $p \in S$ such that all $p_{ij} = y_i p y_j$ are nonzero with controlled overlap structure; let $P = (p_{ij})$ and $D = C/P$.

nodes.name: Compute chain generating function $C^D$
nodes.statement: Show every chain in $C'$ has the form $c_1 p c_2 p \dots p c_n$ with $c_i \in C^B$, then sum: $C'(s,t) = \sum_{i \geq 1} (s t^b)^i C^B(s,t)^{i+1} = (s t^b C^B(s,t)^2)/(1 - s t^b C^B(s,t))$.

nodes.name: Existence of well-positioned monomial $p$
nodes.statement: Let $A, B$ be connected monomial algebras with $\dim_k B \geq 3$, $B$ minimally generated by $Y = \{y_i\}_{i \in \Gamma}$, and $S$ a monomial ideal in $C = A \ast B$. Then $S$ contains a nonzero monomial $p$ such that all $p_{ij} = y_i p y_j$ are nonzero, no overlaps occur for $j \neq k$, and the unique overlap $y_j$ occurs when $j = k$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 16
nodes.statement: Choose a nonzero monomial $n = x n' x \in S$ with $x \in X$. Case 1 ($\#Y = 1$): with $y^2 \neq 0$, set $p = y(x y^2)^q n_1 (yx)^q$ with $q$ large; analyze possible overlaps via the equation $p_{11} = c a = a d$ to derive contradictions. Case 2 ($\#Y \geq 2$): set $p = (x y_1)^q n (y_2 x)^q$; if a long overlap existed, $\{p\}$ would fail to be combinatorially free, contradicting [HL, Prop. 3.15] which forces $p = a b a$ with $\mathrm{len}\, a \geq 4q$.

nodes.name: Choose seed monomial $n = x n' x$
nodes.statement: Since $S$ is a monomial ideal containing the principal ideal generated by $m$, there exists a nonzero monomial $n \in S$ of the form $n = x n' x$ with $x \in X$.

nodes.name: Case 1: $\#Y = 1$
nodes.statement: With $Y = \{y\}$, $\dim B \geq 3$ gives $y^2 \neq 0$. Choose largest $l \geq 0$ with $n = (xy^2)^l n_1$, set $p = y(xy^2)^q n_1 (yx)^q$, $q > \max\{l, \mathrm{len}\, n_1 + 3\}$, then $p_{11} = y^2 (xy^2)^q n_1 (yx)^q y$, and overlap analysis using maximality of $l$ rules out long overlaps.

nodes.name: Case 2: $\#Y \geq 2$
nodes.statement: Set $p = (x y_1)^q n (y_2 x)^q$ with $q > \mathrm{len}\, n$. A long overlap would yield $p = aba$ with $a = (x y_1)^q c (y_2 x)^q$ via [HL, Prop. 3.15], forcing $\mathrm{len}\, p \geq 8q$, contradicting the construction.

nodes.name: Algebras containing a strongly free set are extremal
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be a connected algebra with $r(A) > 0$. If $A$ contains a strongly free set, then $A$ is extremal.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 17
nodes.statement: By [A1, Lemma 2.7] there exists a strongly free element $f$. If $A = k\langle f\rangle$, every proper quotient is finite-dimensional, so $A$ is extremal. Otherwise $B = A/(f)$ is non-trivial and $C = B \ast k\langle g\mid \deg g = \deg f\rangle$ is extremal by Theorem 15. Use the Anick isomorphism $\rho: C \to A$ and ideal comparison $\rho(K) \subset J$ to deduce $r(A/I) \geq r(A/J) \geq r(C/K) > r(C) = r(A)$.

nodes.name: Free-product comparison: $r(A) \geq r(C)$
nodes.section: 6 How a quotient algebra may grow?
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be a connected algebra with $r(A) > 0$, $S \subset A$ a non-empty homogeneous set minimally generating $I = ASA$, $B = A/I$, $C = B \ast k\langle S\rangle$. Then $r(A) \geq r(C)$, with equality iff $S$ is strongly free.

nodes.name: Generalized Govorov inequality
nodes.section: 6 How a quotient algebra may grow?
nodes.statement: Under the notation above, $B(r(A)) S(r(A)) \geq 1$, and the following are equivalent: (i) equality holds; (ii) $r(A) = r(C)$; (iii) $S \subset A$ is strongly free. In particular, if $S$ has $t$ elements of degree $l$, then $t \geq B(r(A))^{-1} r(A)^{-l}$, with equality iff $S$ is strongly free; this generalizes Govorov's inequality (3).
conclusions: $t \geq B(r(A))^{-1} r(A)^{-l}$ when $S$ has $t$ elements of degree $l$

nodes.name: Undecidability of $r(C) = 1/s$
nodes.section: 6 How a quotient algebra may grow?
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{char}\, k = 0$, $A$ is free of rank $s$, $\alpha$ has $t$ quadratic elements, and $(s,t)$ is undecidable, then $C$ is finitely presented and connected (but non-standard) and there is no algorithm to decide whether $r(C) = 1/s$.
